idiom_name: elvis early return (?: return) plus require/check precondition functions
implementation_notes: Kotlin absorbs the guard into expressions and the standard library: value ?: return default exits the function when the value is null, and the precondition functions documented on the Kotlin exception page split the categories - require/requireNotNull throw IllegalArgumentException for caller input, check/checkNotNull throw IllegalStateException for object state, and error()/TODO() mark impossible branches (error returns Nothing, so it fits any expected type). Combining takeIf with ?: keeps a conditional check in the same early-exit shape. The classic if (!ok) return remains right when the failure branch does more than exit; assert() is JVM-only and enabled just with -ea.
pitfalls: ?: return inside a lambda exits the lambda, not the enclosing function; non-local exits only work through inline functions (let, also, run) and otherwise need a label.
require and check throw unchecked exceptions, so the failure is invisible in the signature; when the caller must handle it, return a sealed result or Either instead.
Checking state too early (before the object is configured) turns a legitimate later state into an IllegalStateException; guard at the point of use.
